children: Mutual Housing California's Fairview Terrace will help income-qualified older adults in San Joaquin County find stable, affordable housing and remain connected to the community they call home
STOCKTON, Calif., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire-HISPANIC PR WIRE/ --
, one of California's most experienced Medi-Cal managed care health plans and company of
(NYSE: CNC), announced a $3 million grant to
to support the development of Fairview Terrace, a new affordable housing community for income-qualified seniors in Stockton.

Located at 2222 S. Airport Way, Fairview Terrace will provide 76 affordable homes for adults aged 55 and older. The development will serve households earning up to $58,380, according to 2026 CTCAC income limits. By transforming a long-vacant parcel, Fairview Terrace help address the growing need for affordable housing for older adults in San Joaquin County.

"A safe, affordable place to call home can make a meaningful difference in a person's health and well-being, especially for older adults living on fixed incomes," said Amber Kemp, Vice President, Medi-Cal Strategy, Execution, and Engagement at Health Net. "Fairview Terrace represents more than housing. It offers Stockton seniors the stability, dignity and sense of community that help people stay healthy and connected. We're proud to partner with Mutual Housing California to create a welcoming place where residents can build relationships, access support and thrive for years to come."

The investment will help complete the project's construction financing, supporting the development as it looks to complete the setting of all 76 home modules at the site in 2026, with an anticipated completion planned for 2027. Health Net's grant helps close a funding gap and moves the project one step closer to completion.

"Fairview Terrace will expand housing options for older adults and help ensure more seniors can remain in the community they call home," said San Joaquin County Supervisor Mario Gardea. "This development reflects what can be accomplished when organizations come together around a shared goal, and we're grateful to Health Net and Mutual Housing California for investing in Stockton's future."

"Health Net's $3 million investment is helping turn an ambitious vision into 76 affordable homes for generations of Stockton seniors," said Craig Adelman, CEO of Mutual Housing California. "Having a partner investing in our work creating housing as an essential solution to better health is making the difference in getting healthy communities built. Fairview Terrace pairs that collaboration with an innovative construction approach that delivers these homes faster, giving older adults the stability and opportunity to remain connected to the community they call home."

Fairview Terrace is one of many community investments Health Net has supported throughout California to improve the conditions that shape health and wellbeing. Over the last five years, Health Net has committed more than $284 million to community-based initiatives that address social factors such as housing, food access and community health. Through these partnerships, Health Net continues to invest in solutions that help people build healthier, more stable lives.
In Sacramento and San Joaquin counties, Health Net has invested a combined
$11 million
in affordable housing and related initiatives, including:
Sacramento County — $3 million:
Green Means Go/Sacramento Area Council of Governments (SACOG), $2 million; and San Juan Apartments II/Mutual Housing, $1 million.
San Joaquin County — $8 million:
Fairview Terrace/Mutual Housing, $3 million; San Joaquin Affordable Housing Trust, $3 million; and Lodi Seniors at Salas Park, $2 million.
Through investments like Fairview Terrace, Health Net is helping expand affordable housing options for older adults and strengthen communities across the region.
About Health Net
